findings.title: Silence menu item does nothing in the new list view
findings.body:
AlertRuleMenu now shows "Silence notifications" for Grafana prom rules, because `canSilence` is ORed with `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. Clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`.

The drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true. In the list view (GrafanaGroupLoader and FilterView), `rule` (the ruler rule) is now always undefined, so the drawer never opens.

Users with silence permissions see a menu item that silently does nothing. The new test only asserts the item exists and never clicks it. The drawer needs to work from the prom rule, or the item should be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: Delete and Pause actions are lost in the list view despite being computed from promRule
findings.body:
`canDelete` and `canPause` are now ORed with the Grafana prom-rule abilities. However, the menu items are still gated on the ruler rule:
- `canDelete && rulerRule`
- `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`

RuleActionsButtons.V2 no longer passes a ruler rule in the list view. As a result, users with delete or update permissions on the folder can no longer delete or pause/resume rules from the list. Previously they could, because the ruler rule was fetched.

The prom-based Delete/Pause abilities are effectively dead code. GrafanaGroupLoader.test ("exactly 4 menu items" while granting AlertingRuleDelete) locks this regression in. Either support delete/pause from the prom rule (fetch the ruler rule lazily on click) or stop computing these abilities from promRule.

findings.title: skipToken path returns Duplicate as supported+allowed, leaking into non-Grafana rules
findings.body:
When `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gets `skipToken`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)` runs. Then `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` and `duplicateSupported = true`.

`Duplicate` therefore becomes `[true, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]` even though there is no rule.

AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler ability. For data-source rules (Mimir/Loki/vanilla Prometheus), or any case where `promRule` is not a Grafana rule, the Duplicate item now appears for any user with Grafana `alert.rules:create`. This happens even when the ruler is unavailable or the user lacks external-rule write permission.

The skip case should return all-NotSupported abilities. The RulesTable cloud-rule tests miss this because `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` is mocked to always return `[false,false]`.

findings.title: Federated rule groups no longer treated as immutable in legacy ability hook
findings.body:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities(CombinedRule)` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and marked federated Mimir groups as immutable, so Update, Delete and Pause were not supported.

It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO. Every consumer of `useAlertRuleAbility`/`useAlertRuleAbilities` (legacy rule list, RuleDetails, rule viewer actions) will now offer Edit/Delete on federated rule groups.

That is a behavioural regression. Editing such groups through the UI is unsupported and can drop `source_tenants`. The federated check should be preserved, e.g. by passing the group or computing it in the CombinedRule wrapper.

findings.title: Missing React key on GrafanaRuleListItem in rules.map
findings.body:
The previous `GrafanaRuleLoader` was rendered with `key={key}`. The replacement `<GrafanaRuleListItem ... />` inside `rules.map(...)` has no `key` prop, even though `key` is destructured right above and used for the other branches.

Consequences:
- React emits a missing-key warning.
- Reconciliation falls back to index, which can mix up component state (open menus, delete modals, silence drawer state) between items.

Add `key={key}`.

findings.title: Rule view link lost the returnTo parameter
findings.body:
The removed implementation built the link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo: createReturnTo() })`. The new component drops `returnTo`.

Navigating from the (filtered) list to a rule's detail page no longer returns the user to the same list/filter state via the back/return link. This is a UX regression unrelated to removing the ruler request.

findings.title: Prom-based abilities exclude Grafana recording rules from Export/Pause, unlike the ruler version
findings.body:
In `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, `ModifyExport`, `Pause` and `Restore` are gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which includes Grafana recording rules.

The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` gates them on `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`. So Grafana-managed recording rules lose Export (and Pause) in the list view, while they keep them in the rule viewer, where the ruler rule is available.

The two ability sources should agree. Use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these actions.

findings.title: Provisioned detection for prom rules depends on a field not added server-side in this PR
findings.body:
`isProvisionedPromRule` relies on the newly typed `provenance` field of `GrafanaPromRuleDTO`. The list view now uses it to decide whether Edit, Update and Delete are immutable, and AlertRuleMenu ORs it with the ruler result.

This PR changes no backend code. If the Grafana Prometheus-compatible rules endpoint does not serialize `provenance`, provisioned rules will be reported as mutable: the Edit button will show for them in the list. Because of the OR, ruler-side immutability can also be overridden in the rule viewer.

Please confirm the API returns this field, or add backend support and a test.

findings.title: Legacy ability hook can now throw during render via groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule
findings.body:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously derived the source name with `getRulesSourceName`, which never throws. It now calls `groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule(rule)`.

For data-source rules that function resolves the datasource UID and throws when the datasource cannot be found. That is why the tests had to be changed to pass a real `mimirDs`.

Any CombinedRule whose rulesSource isn't resolvable (e.g. a removed or renamed datasource, or test fixtures) now crashes the component tree instead of degrading gracefully.

findings.title: Stale docstring still says the group is loaded from Ruler endpoints
findings.body:
The component comment still reads "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints." The `expectedRulesCount` prop doc also still refers to the Ruler response.

The Ruler query was removed in this PR and only the Prometheus endpoint is used. The comments should be updated to avoid misleading future maintainers.
